title: A pressure vacuum breaker is the raised, testable irrigation assembly
description: Identify a PVB by its bonnet, air inlet, shutoffs, test cocks, elevation, and irrigation placement before diagnosing leaks or freeze damage.
prompt: Which PVB clue do you see?
answer: A PVB protects against backsiphonage and is commonly used on irrigation. It is testable and can remain under pressure, unlike a basic atmospheric vacuum breaker.
urgency: Never cap the air inlet. Active discharge, a cracked bonnet, or freeze damage needs isolation through the correct procedure and qualified service.
diagramAlt: Pressure vacuum breaker with inlet, outlet, test cocks, bonnet, and air inlet labeled
identifiers: Two shutoff valves and test cocks indicate a testable assembly.
The bonnet and air inlet sit above the main body.
The installation is usually elevated above downstream irrigation piping.

choices.label: Water comes from the bonnet

choices.label: The body is intact but testing is due
choices.detail: Check the utility and accepted tester route.

notThisDevice: An AVB normally has no field test cocks.
A hose-bib breaker threads directly to a faucet.
An RPZ has a relief zone below an inline body.
evidenceNote: Manufacturer installation instructions and local plumbing or utility rules control elevation, testing, and service.
